title: anchor-fragment-rewrite-and-stable-toolcall-handshake
author: Priya Desai
description: Motivation: intermittent partial-JSON emissions and out-of-order tool/function-call handoffs observed under backpressure for long-running SSE responses. This PR adds an explicit anchor-checkpointing approach to SSE fragment emission and rewrites delimiter handling to normalize mixed newline/\r sequences, while ensuring that function-call sentinel frames are fenced until the prior JSON span is fully committed. Key goals: 1) avoid emitting partial JSON slices that cannot be reassembled by OpenAI-compatible clients; 2) prevent toolcall tokens from leaking into earlier fragments during stream replay; 3) retain backwards compatibility with existing OpenAI-compat framing but make the reassembly deterministic under retries and replays. Implementation summary: (a) introduce an anchor sequence id (anchor_seq) embedded as a lightweight header on emitted SSE frames to allow receivers to latch reassembly windows and ignore stale fragments; (b) implement delimiter normalization and an escape-folding pass that collapses mixed CR/LF runs into a canonical \n boundary and preserves deliberate \r markers inside strings; (c) implement a "function-call fence" state in the SSE emitter so that function-call sentinel lines are only emitted once the emitter observes the anchor checkpoint acknowledged (or after a configurable flush timeout for best-effort clients); (d) add a replay-safe checksum tag for mid-json spans (optional) so clients can validate and request retransmit if available. Compatibility notes: behavior defaults to previous framing for clients that do not inspect anchor_seq but improves determinism for our OpenAI-compat layer and downstream SDKs. The PR includes unit and integration tests exercising backpressure, fragmentation, and replay scenarios, plus a short doc snippet explaining the anchor semantics for SDK consumers. Rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag sse_anchor_enable (off by default for 48 hours), will be enabled cluster-wide after canary verification. Related: ENG-2412 (stream-stability spike), SUP-9981 (customer incident resulting in partial JSON).
commits: 1) 9b1f2d3: add anchor_seq header to sse emitter and parser with tests; 2) a3c4f55: normalize delimiters and add escape-folding pass; 3) f7e8a90: introduce function-call fence and configurable flush timeout; 4) 2c3d444: add integration tests for replay and backpressure scenarios; 5) 7d9a1b0: docs and release-notes entry
review_conversation: Ethan Park: Can you explain how anchor_seq is exposed in the public wire format? Priya Desai: anchor_seq is an optional header line (e.g. "event: anchor_seq=12345") in the SSE envelope; it is benign for older clients and consumed by updated parsers. Marta Novak: I saw the integration flake on replays where the checksum mismatches; is that expected? Priya Desai: The checksum is optional and only emitted when runtime flag sse_anchor_checksum=true; tests were updated to cover both code paths. Liam Zhou: The function-call fence timeout default seems long (3s) — could we reduce? Priya Desai: Reduced default to 250ms after perf review; left configurable per-workload. Ethan Park: LGTM after nits. Marta Novak: approved. QA: flaky test removed; CI green on rerun.
release_notes: stabilize SSE framing by adding anchor_seq header for deterministic fragment reassembly; normalize CR/LF delimiters; introduce function-call fencing to prevent toolcall token leakage across fragments; feature gated behind sse_anchor_enable.
notes_for_ops: Enable sse_anchor_enable=false on prod prior to rollout; perform a 2-node canary with sse_anchor_enable=true and monitor streaming error-rate and function-call drop metrics (streaming.partial_json.error, streaming.toolcall.drop). Rollback by toggling feature flag and restarting the emitter pods if we observe regressions.
testing_summary: Added unit tests for parser reassembly, emitter sequence semantics, and delimiter normalization. Integration harness simulates packet splits, backpressure and replay; added a deterministic test that reproduces the customer incident SUP-9981. e2e canary executed against a staging cluster with 10k simulated concurrent streams.
